newsitem.title: SLOVAKIA: Slovak blue chips open week mixed, SAX up 0.98.
newsitem.headline: Slovak blue chips open week mixed, SAX up 0.98.

text.p: Slovak blue chips opened the week mixed in moderate trading on the Bratislava Stock Exchange (BSE) on Monday, as the SAX index edged up 0.98 points to 203.53.
Oil and gas storage company Nafta dominated the session with two blocks totalling 19,500 shares changing hands. Nafta closed down 25 at 2,000 crowns.

Brokers said that foreign investors appeared to be selling off of their holdings in Nafta after the state sold off its 49.5 percent stake in the firm to the little-known Druha Obchodna a.s., for a price far below the market value.
The new owner had to pay 500 million crowns, while on the Bratislava Stock Exchange the stake was worth around 3.2 billion crowns.
"The development seems to be fulfiling our expectations that Nafta shares are slowly returning from abroad back to Slovakia," said Patrik Granec of Slovenska Sporitelna.
Steel maker VSZ closed unchanged at 620 crowns.
Slovakia's largest commercial bank VUB was the only blue chip to post slight gains, moving up 20 to 1,620 crowns.
Oil refiner Slovnaft fell 14 crowns to close at 931, with brokers saying an unidentified investor was testing the bid floor before entering the market for a larger purchase.
Overall volume decreased to 257,358 shares, from 781,328 shares traded on Friday. Turnover fell to 166.85 million crowns, from 610.50 million on Friday.
